message.reasoning_content:
Key risk: FP32 rational approximation vs 1e-6 absolute tolerance. Cephes atan double accuracy ~1e-16; FP32 adaptation with tl.where(pick) approximations — note original Cephes numerator coefficients are -0.8751? Actually Cephes atan double coefficients: p = {-8.75060860003190412272e-01, -1.6157537187333650766e+01, -7.500855792314704669e+01, -1.22886668449013666e+02, -6.4850219049420253e+01} and q = {2.485e+01, 1.6500e+02, 4.3285e+02, 4.8534e+02, 1.9460e+02}. So coefficients match (rounded to 4 sig figs: -16.16 vs -16.157...). The rounding to short decimals plus FP32 arithmetic may exceed 1e-6 absolute tolerance. Also reciprocal uses -1/max(mag,1) — for upper branch mag>2.414 so max is mag, fine. But note angle for upper: pi/2 - atan(1/x)... value = pi/2 + atan(reduced) where reduced=-1/x, so value = pi/2 - atan(1/x) = atan(x). OK.

Also reciprocal computed unconditionally with tl.maximum(magnitude,1.0) — safe (no div by zero).

Risk: FP32 accumulation error of polynomial in square; square up to 1 (reduced ≤1). Relative error ~1e-7 times... may reach ~1e-6 boundary. Also coefficient rounding (-64.85 vs -64.852... etc.) introduces relative ~1e-4 error in correction term? correction ≈ reduced*square*num/den; relative error in coefficients ~1e-5-ish yields absolute error in angle ~1e-6ish. This is the designed suspect.
